The new commits fix the empty-slice divide-by-zero in `average`, but the newly added `first` function has the same class of bug the sibling `last` function guards against: it indexes without bounds handling and panics when `n` exceeds the slice length.

- `src/lib.rs:8-10` — the empty-slice early return fixes prior finding `f-divide-by-zero`; I'm marking it fixed.
- `src/lib.rs:16` — `&items[..n]` panics for `n > items.len()`, while `last` at `src/lib.rs:3` deliberately saturates and documents the "fewer than n" case. The doc comment on `first` doesn't mention a panic either.
- The dropped `f-integer-division` finding stays dropped.

draftedFindings.body: `&items[..n]` is an out-of-bounds slice index when `n > items.len()`, so `first(&[1, 2], 5)` panics. The sibling `last` function (`src/lib.rs:3`) deliberately avoids this with `items.len().saturating_sub(n)` and documents the fewer-than-`n` case; `first` should be consistent. Use `&items[..n.min(items.len())]` and mention the clamping behavior in the doc comment, mirroring `last`.
